# M3 optional collection modules

Copyright 2026 Hitesh Soliwal and contributors. SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0.

This pack exposes the qualified Synexia filtered and sorted views with M3JDK-owned names. It builds the existing primitive collection module from its original sources and adds a separate optional module for generic views and versioned primitive row projections. The classes need no Synexia runtime dependency.

| Module | Public owner | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `jdk.m3.collections` | `jdk.m3.collections.M3FilteredViews` | Read-only live collection, set, sorted/navigable set, and sorted/navigable map views. Backing order, predicate calls and exceptions remain authoritative. |
| `jdk.m3.collections` | `jdk.m3.collections.M3MutableFilteredViews` | Live mutable navigable set/map views with predicate admission, visible-only mutation and existing key-set restrictions. |
| `jdk.m3.collections` | `com.m3.util.M3PrimitiveIndexView` and `M3PrimitiveSoaStore` | Ordered row projections over typed primitive lanes. Views detect source-generation changes; exported arrays are defensive copies. Full-match filters reuse only a newly allocated private result array. |
| `jdk.m3.collections` | Existing `com.m3.util.M3PrimitiveKind` and `M3DenseHash` | The original source owners are compiled in place. `M3SortableTopK` and `M3RuntimeHeap` retain their donor policies after package projection. |
| `com.m3.collections` | Existing primitive collections, `M3LongFilteredView`, `M3LongSortedViews`, and `M3IndexMaskCompactor` | The complete existing module is compiled unchanged. Its detached mask selector uses an explicitly requested Java or native backend. |

The row-view filter and detached native mask selector have different mask and lifetime contracts. The row view preserves signed integer masks and source-version checks; the native selector admits only unsigned byte masks against detached aligned arrays. No implicit dispatch or alias joins these APIs.

## Build and qualify

Use a Java 21 development toolchain. The Maven POM defaults to the repository's source-built JUnit coordinate. Build those existing test-support modules before running its three JUnit entry points:

```sh
mvn -f m3/tooling/module-packs/collections/pom.xml clean verify
```

The standalone Linux image proof requires Python 3, a C17 compiler and `nm`. It has no Maven dependency:

```sh
python3 m3/tooling/module-packs/collections/build.py \
  --jdk-home /absolute/path/to/jdk-21 \
  --repo-root /absolute/path/to/M3JDK21 \
  --out /absolute/path/to/fresh/collections-proof
```

The optional Maven profile `m3-collections-image` invokes the same script at `verify`. Use `clean verify` so the required output directory is fresh. The script compiles both named modules, generates the existing native header with `javac -h`, compiles the unchanged native peer and checks its exact JNI export. It runs the three projected contract mains and the original `M3IndexMaskCompactorSelfTest --native` on the host with `-Xcheck:jni`.

It then delegates to the existing `m3/tooling/jmod-recipes/tools/jmod_pack.py`, attaching `libm3_collections_mask.so` to its declaring module. The packager creates two JMODs and links a development image. The script repeats all four oracles on that image, verifies that the image contains the identical native library, and writes a source/hash receipt and a `M3_COLLECTIONS_PACK_PROOF.json` result. JMODs are linking inputs; use the modular JARs or the linked image to run applications.

For a modular JAR consumer, add `requires jdk.m3.collections;` to its descriptor and place `jdk.m3.collections.jar` on the module path. The new facade package can be used directly:

```java
NavigableSet<Integer> visible = M3FilteredViews.filter(backing, value -> value % 2 == 0);
```

Use the separate `com.m3.collections` module when its primitive owners are needed. The two modules have disjoint packages. The native library is optional outside the explicit native qualification: `NATIVE_REQUIRED` fails when the existing peer is unavailable.

## Compatibility and evidence

Canonical source and portable recipes remain in `hsoliwal/com.synexia`; this repository owns the target packages and M3 names. `PROJECTION_SOURCE_IDENTITY.json` records exact donor and target hashes. The read-only facade includes two qualified private wrapper-construction reductions. The row view includes exact-fit array reuse in its two filter methods. These are separate, tested source changes; the remaining projection is package/type renaming plus rights notices and documentation links.

Null-permitting navigable sets have the donor's existing null-sentinel ambiguity. Independent probes also retain existing bounded-range mutable-navigation counterexamples. These limitations are recorded rather than silently changed by a performance patch. The standalone donor evidence covers the additional legacy wrapper and primitive-long families without treating them as aliases of the new facades.

This separately built Apache module does not advance the repository's ordered receiving sequence or replace `java.util`. The optional module/JNI/image proof is bounded to the executed platform and toolchain. Full custom HotSpot builds, jtreg, interpreter/C1/C2, CDS and broader workload/resource gates remain separate acceptance work.
